title: Functions and arguments
outcome: Trace functions and arguments and explain the changed program before running it.
scenario: Match arguments to parameters. A function prints the difference between capacity and reserved spaces.
given: Python 3: def show_free(capacity,reserved): print(capacity-reserved). Calls: show_free(11,3); show_free(3,11).

steps.label: Define without calling
steps.detail: The definition creates the function but prints nothing yet.

steps.label: Match first arguments
steps.detail: capacity=11 and reserved=3 give a printed 8.

steps.label: Trace reversed call
steps.detail: capacity=3 and reserved=11 give -8 under the same arithmetic.

explanation: Positional arguments match parameter names in order. A function definition is not an execution of its body; separate calls supply separate input values.

counterfactual.change: Remove both calls and leave the definition only.
counterfactual.reason: The body runs only when the function is called.

student_task: Match every argument to a parameter for the two calls. Why do outputs differ, and what prints when both calls are removed?
teacher_answer: The first call binds 11 to capacity and 3 to reserved, printing 8. The second reverses those bindings and prints -8. A definition with no calls prints nothing.
project_evidence: For Python readiness before the Responsible Plant Classifier, retain a trace of the values, the predicted outputs and the changed-case explanation. Use actual Python 3 results to check the prediction after reasoning first.
limits: The arithmetic permits negative results; a real capacity contract may reject reserved>capacity instead of treating it as free space.
review_note: Individually authored supported practice; distinct from the reserved independent case. Python semantics are checked on standalone snippets; no learned model or real pupil result is implied.
